items.prompt: Some fractions can be written as whole numbers. Some fractions cannot be expressed as whole numbers. How do we know if a fraction can be written as a whole number?
items.expected: the times table of the bottom number
items.demo: Well, if the top number is in *the times table of the bottom number*, then the fraction can be written as a whole number.

items.prompt: For example, can thirty-one over ten be written as a whole number?
items.demo: *No*. How do I know? Because thirty-one is not in the ten times table.

items.prompt: Can thirty over ten be written as a whole number?
items.demo: *Yes*. How do I know? Because thirty is in the ten times table. Ten times thirty is thirty.

items.prompt: Can thirty over five be written as a whole number?
items.demo: *Yes*. How do I know? Because thirty is in the five times table. Five times six is thirty.

items.prompt: Can twenty over five be written as a whole number?
items.demo: *Yes*. How do I know? Because twenty is in the five times table, five times four is twenty.

items.prompt: Can twenty over six be written as a whole number?
items.demo: *No*. How do I know? Because twenty is not in the six times table.
